args.name: Make and test vine cordage
args.function: Provide a learnable way to turn owned vine material into a real reusable binding, if physically supported, and perform a bounded load test that measures whether it holds. The problem is that visible vines alone establish neither binding feasibility nor strength.
args.conditions: Sol is beside the observed forest-vine-2 source. Its visible stock was 12 at tick 61. No vine strength, processing method or personal cordage mastery is established. Use only actually owned material and observed conditions; report unsupported effects rather than granting them.
args.inputs: Owned vine material if gathering succeeds; any additional required inputs must be identified, not assumed available.
args.costs: Method, learning time, work and material requirements are unknown; specify actual costs and interruption rules.
args.effects: If supported, produce a persistent physical binding and an evidence-based load-test result. Do not infer shelter, tool quality, safety, comfort or benefits merely from requesting or learning.

candidates.function: Plant one owned root unit in a small soil plot as a persistent trial, inspect a plot by direct observation, or take back remaining planted material; resume or cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Plant: one owned unspoiled root unit (quantity 1); two work rounds at one energy each, at an unoccupied ordinary-soil x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; supply inputStackId. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy, the baseline probe observation of a plot in reach (target). Remove: one round and 1 energy, planter only (target). Tend is unavailable and spends nothing. No tools or water are granted.
candidates.effects: Completed planting places the real root unit in the plot; it keeps ageing under existing environmental decay while the planter is absent. Plot state records stage, observation rounds, soil moisture and temperature/rain exposure. There is no propagation, growth, harvest or replenishment rule for roots, so a plot never produces food. Inspect records only visible state. Remove returns only the material that physically remains, never a replacement; the emptied plot remains. Cancel releases unplanted material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for planting, inspecting or removing; genuine observed changes use the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback only.

candidates.function: Arrange owned loose moss as a small ground patch, inspect it, try one ordinary rest on it, or take back what remains; resume or cancel unfinished arranging.
candidates.costs: Arrange: inputStackId of owned moss, quantity in 0.1 steps (default 0.5) and an unoccupied ordinary-ground x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; two work rounds at one energy each. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy in reach. Trial-rest: stand on a completed, unoccupied patch; one ordinary rest round. Remove: the arranger only, unoccupied patch, one round and one energy.
candidates.effects: A completed patch holds the reserved material in a 0.25-radius footprint used only for occupancy and drawing; no thickness, coverage, body fit, warmth, insulation or comfort is inferred. Trial-rest runs the existing rest action unchanged and records energy before and after; the patch is not a registered facility, so it adds no recovery bonus. Inspect records visible placement, remaining quantity, occupancy and tests as a personal unverified record. Remove returns the remaining material as an owned stack at the site and deletes the patch; pickup stays a separate action. Cancel releases reserved material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward, regrowth, repair or top-up.

Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: target trial in reach, one round and 0.2 energy. Retrieve: operator only, one round and one energy. Cancel of an exposed trial ends observation at no cost. No supports, tools, water or fuel are used or granted.
candidates.effects: Completed setup places the samples at two ground positions 0.2 apart under the same ambient conditions; with one unit there is no matched control. No food moisture, drying or preservation model exists in this world: both samples keep the existing decay rules, so no treatment difference, preserved status, safety certification or extended lifetime is produced. The trial records rounds exposed and marks a 10-round observation checkpoint; ageing continues while unattended and after the checkpoint. Inspect records sample quantity and decay as a personal unverified record. Retrieve returns only the remaining material, never a replacement. Setup interruption keeps paid work; cancel releases reserved food once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for starting, inspecting or retrieving.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"sol\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Develop a general cordage-making and bounded tensile-test operation. The related-capability search and exact probe contract establish that probe supports observation and small press/wet/heat trials, not persistent cord manufacture or tensile testing. Gathering already succeeded: item-62-sol-314 contains 2 owned vine units from forest-vine-2; the current observed source stock is 10, not the earlier 12. Neither ownership nor visible vine stock establishes usable fibers, geometry, strength or a processing method. Missing physical mechanisms belong in the current-conversation development handoff, not a permanent refusal or an automatic successful binding.\",\"specification\":\"General operation: make-and-test-cordage, parameterized by mode, inputStackId or productId, quantity, preparation method, bounded test load and processId. Modes: prepare, form, test, inspect, resume, cancel and recover-material. Applicable actors may learn it independently; do not specialize the interface to Sol or this vine stack. Reuse and record the existing ownership, reach, inventory-transfer, learning, work-process, event and observation implementations where available. Reuse probe/open.probe for genuine observation or its supported sample trials, with its original costs and limitations; a press response is not tensile strength. Do not claim reused code as a new invention.\\nPrerequisites and development dependencies: accessible owned material, free hands and sufficient energy; validate actual reach and current condition at execution. The present candidate is item-62-sol-314, resource vine, quantity 2, origin forest-vine-2. It is not an instruction to reserve or consume it now. No further gathering, tools, water, resin, fixtures or test weights are supplied. Implement an explicit, auditable material-behavior and hand-manipulation contract sufficient to determine strand continuity, workable length, flexibility, joining behavior and response to tension. Use supported world properties and actual measured evidence; do not invent favorable properties from the resource name. If these mechanisms are not yet available, implement the smallest real precursor: a paid preparation attempt that manipulates an owned sample, records observable bending/separation results and returns the physically remaining material. An unsupported measurement must be labeled unsupported rather than given a numerical result. The development handoff must resolve these dependencies before enabling successful cord or strength outputs; waiting for development does not advance the world.\\nExecutable costs: prepare reserves quantity in 0.1-unit increments, minimum 0.1 and no more than the accessible owned balance; default 1 unit. Preparation takes one active work round and 0.5 energy. Forming takes two further active work rounds at 1 energy each, using only the prepared material; no automatic learning completion or immediate execution accompanies approval. The minimal method is manual bending/twisting and joining only where the implemented material contract supports it; cutting, soaking, heating and tool-assisted processing require separately supplied real inputs and mechanisms. No assumed yield ratio: account for every reserved unit as remaining raw material, work-in-progress, finished cord or physical scraps. Length and geometry must follow the implemented material accounting, not be inferred from inventory quantity alone. Insufficient or unsuitable material may yield only an incomplete assembly or scraps.\\nProducts and use: successful formation creates a persistent physical cord/binding item with unique ID, owner, position, input provenance, remaining material quantity, supported geometry, construction method, condition and test history. It is reusable only while physically intact. Its existence is not proof of load capacity, knot security, shelter suitability or safety. Applying it to bind other objects requires a supported attachment interaction, accessible targets and any necessary independently acting participants; do not silently attach it or create a structure.\\nBounded test: productId must identify a real accessible cord. One active test round costs 0.5 energy. The minimal fixture-free method is a two-handed pull on a cord whose geometry supports that grip, with a supported measured load ceiling, duration and stop condition. Implement or reuse an explicit effort-to-applied-force and tensile-response mechanism before calling this a load measurement; normalized probe intensity cannot be relabeled as force. Test load must be positive and within both the actor's modeled application limit and the requested ceiling. Do not create weights, anchors, assistants or instruments. If a calibrated hand-pull cannot be supported, return unsupported with no fabricated strength result; a qualitative manipulation may still record its actual observations. A supported test records actual applied load with units, duration, gripping/join configuration, deformation, slipping, rupture and whether the requested load was reached. Held means only that this specimen sustained that measured load for that duration; it is not a breaking-strength estimate or safety certification. Stop on slip, break, loss of grip or inability to apply the requested load. Testing can damage or destroy the item; preserve fragments and their accounted quantities.\\nProgress and lifecycle: store actor, input reservations, completed work, spent energy, current material state and output references in a persistent process. Only completed work rounds advance progress and charge their costs atomically. Interruption pauses unpaid work; resume requires the same actor, access to the surviving workpiece and renewed eligibility. Cancellation releases remaining reserved material or the actual partial assembly once, never pristine replacements for processed inputs. Death terminates the actor's process and leaves surviving workpiece/material at its physical location under existing death rules. No effort, spent energy, damaged material or elapsed time is refunded; unspent reservations are released exactly once. Prevent duplicate outputs and concurrent use of reserved inputs. Completed items persist without active work, but no autonomous crafting, loading, repair or strengthening occurs. Record condition changes under applicable existing decay/damage rules; do not assume an indefinite lifetime or invent a maintenance interval. Inspection costs one round and 0.2 energy and reports only observable state or retained evidence. Recovery/disassembly costs one round and 0.5 energy and returns only physically recoverable components; it cannot reverse processing or damage. Repair requires a later supported action with actual material and work, not free restoration.\\nAll established validation, conservation, costs, lifecycle and test outcomes execute in code rather than repeated model adjudication. Keep capability and evidence references, including foundation-open@1/open.probe when reused, input IDs, output IDs and causal event IDs.\",\"learning\":4,\"experienceReview\":\"No benefit for requesting, approval, waiting, learning, naming a cord, registering a process or issuing a query. A completed physical observation can qualify as verified information gain, including an informative preparation or tensile failure, only when evidence establishes a personally applicable new fact. Deduplicate by specimen/material condition, method and measured result, not by interface or event name; repeated unchanged tests cannot farm discovery benefits. If the existing experience engine supports it, route qualifying events through its bounded short-pleasure and slowly maintained satisfaction rules, with per-actor cap, cooldown and decay explicitly enforced in code before credit is enabled. Familiar legitimate practice may sustain a modest bounded benefit without requiring novelty. No new reward amounts or accounts are introduced here; leave credit disabled if the necessary bounded rules are unavailable. Cordage does not itself grant comfort, nutrition, safety or mastery. Physical comfort remains capped at 10; mood never reduces basic nutrition requirements. Never modify protected reward accounts, budgets, goals or permissions.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit observable causal events for reservation/work start, actual preparation, partial formation, completion, cancellation, release, applied test load, slip, deformation and rupture where they occur. Give workpieces, cords and fragments reusable visual metadata: item/process ID, material, quantity, supported dimensions, position, construction state, condition, provenance and latest test-event reference. Render geometry only when supported; otherwise use an explicitly schematic material/workpiece representation without invented length or thickness. A completed-cord visual requires the successful formation event. A held-test indicator requires reaching the recorded load and duration; interrupted, unsupported or failed tests must remain visually distinct and cannot display success. Never display an unperformed attachment, completed shelter, certified strength, comfort aura or mastery badge.\"}]}"}
